<INSTRUCTIONS>
# External Agent Builder

This repository includes a skill that guides you through building standalone external agent binaries for the [Entire CLI](https://github.com/entireio/cli). The current testing split is:

- Protocol compliance in `external-agents-tests`
- Lifecycle integration in this repo's `e2e/` harness
- Agent-specific unit tests in each `agents/entire-agent-*` module

## Available Commands

| Command | Skill file | Description |
|---------|-----------|-------------|
| Full pipeline | `.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/SKILL.md` | Run all three phases sequentially |
| Research | `.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/research.md` | Analyze the target agent's capabilities and map to the protocol |
| Write tests | `.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/write-tests.md` | Scaffold the binary and wire protocol compliance plus lifecycle coverage |
| Implement | `.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/implement.md` | Build the binary using protocol compliance first, lifecycle second, unit tests last |

## How to Use

When the user asks to "build an external agent", "create an agent binary", or "external agent plugin":

1. Read `.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/SKILL.md` for the full pipeline overview
2. Follow the three phases in order: research, write-tests, implement
3. Each phase has a dedicated skill file with detailed instructions
4. Keep reusable protocol checks out of this repo's `e2e/` directory. Add them to `external-agents-tests` instead.

## Tool Mapping (Codex)

The skill files reference Claude Code tool names. Map them to Codex equivalents:

| Skill references | Codex equivalent |
|-----------------|-----------------|
| `TodoWrite` | `update_plan` |
| `Task` / subagent launches | Codex's native subagent system |
| `Skill` tool | Read the skill file directly |
| `Read`, `Write`, `Edit`, `Glob`, `Grep`, `Bash` | Native Codex tools |

## Protocol Spec

The external agent protocol is defined at:
`https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/main/docs/architecture/external-agent-protocol.md`

</INSTRUCTIONS>

L1: # External Agents for Entire CLI
L2: 
L3: This repository contains standalone external agent binaries that extend the [Entire CLI](https://github.com/entireio/cli) with support for additional AI coding agents.
L4: 
L5: ## What Are External Agents?
L6: 
L7: External agents are standalone binaries (named `entire-agent-<name>`) that teach Entire CLI how to work with AI coding agents it doesn't natively support. When an external agent is installed on your `PATH`, Entire discovers it automatically and gains the ability to:
L8: 
L9: - **Create checkpoints** during AI coding sessions so you can rewind mistakes
L10: - **Capture transcripts** of what the AI agent did and why
L11: - **Install hooks** so the AI agent's lifecycle events (start, stop, commit) flow through Entire
L12: 
L13: External agents communicate with Entire CLI via subcommands that accept and return JSON over stdin/stdout. See the [external agent protocol spec](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/main/docs/architecture/external-agent-protocol.md) for the full interface.
L14: 
L15: ## Available Agents
L16: 
L17: | Agent | Directory | Status |
L18: |-------|-----------|--------|
L19: | [Kiro](agents/entire-agent-kiro/) | `agents/entire-agent-kiro/` | Implemented — hooks + transcript analysis |
L20: | [Amp](agents/entire-agent-amp/) | `agents/entire-agent-amp/` | Implemented — hooks + transcript analysis + token calculation + compact transcripts |
L21: | [LangGraph](agents/entire-agent-langgraph/) | `agents/entire-agent-langgraph/` | Implemented — Python callback bridge + transcript analysis |
L22: | [CrewAI](agents/entire-agent-crewai/) | `agents/entire-agent-crewai/` | Implemented — Python event listener bridge + transcript analysis |
L23: | [Qwen Code](agents/entire-agent-qwen/) | `agents/entire-agent-qwen/` | Implemented — hooks + transcript analysis + compact transcripts |
L24: | [Grok Build](agents/entire-agent-grok/) | `agents/entire-agent-grok/` | Implemented — hooks + transcript analysis + compact transcripts |
L25: | [Oh My Pi](agents/entire-agent-omp/) | `agents/entire-agent-omp/` | Implemented — hooks + transcript analysis + compact transcripts |
L26: | [Kilo](agents/entire-agent-kilo/) | `agents/entire-agent-kilo/` | Implemented (preview) — hooks + transcript analysis + token calculation + compact transcripts |
L27: | [Goose](agents/entire-agent-goose/) | `agents/entire-agent-goose/` | Implemented (preview) — hooks + transcript analysis + token calculation + compact transcripts |
L28: | [Hermes Agent](agents/entire-agent-hermes/) | `agents/entire-agent-hermes/` | Implemented (preview) — sanitized observer hooks + transcript analysis + compact transcripts |
L29: | [Sarvam Code](agents/entire-agent-sarvam/) | `agents/entire-agent-sarvam/` | Implemented (preview) — hooks + transcript analysis + token calculation + compact transcripts |
L30: 
L31: See each agent's own README for setup and usage instructions.
L32: 
L33: ## Enabling External Agents
L34: 
L35: External agent discovery is opt-in. Once an `entire-agent-<name>` binary is on your `PATH`, set `external_agents: true` in the repo's `.entire/settings.json` so Entire scans for it:
L36: 
L37: ```json
L38: {
L39:   "external_agents": true
L40: }
L41: ```
L42: 
L43: Without this flag, Entire ignores external agent binaries even when they're installed.
L44: 
L45: ### LangGraph and CrewAI
L46: 
L47: LangGraph and CrewAI support is provided by the Python package
L48: [`entire-adapter`](https://pypi.org/project/entire-adapter/). These entries
L49: bridge framework lifecycle callbacks into Entire rather than wrapping a
L50: standalone chat CLI.
L51: 
L52: For LangGraph or LangChain projects:
L53: 
L54: ```bash
L55: pip install "entire-adapter[langgraph]"
L56: entire enable --agent langgraph --telemetry=false
L57: ```
L58: 
L59: For CrewAI projects:
L60: 
L61: ```bash
L62: pip install "entire-adapter[crewai]"
L63: entire enable --agent crewai --telemetry=false
L64: ```
L65: 
L66: After enabling, add the adapter to your framework code. LangGraph uses
L67: `EntireCallbackHandler`; CrewAI uses `EntireCrewAIListener`.
L68: 
L69: ### Qwen Code
L70: 
L71: Qwen support targets the terminal `qwen` coding agent:
L72: 
L73: ```bash
L74: cd agents/entire-agent-qwen
L75: mise run build
L76: cp entire-agent-qwen /usr/local/bin/
L77: 
L78: cd /path/to/your/repo
L79: entire enable --agent qwen --telemetry=false
L80: qwen -p "Create hello.txt with hello world" --yolo
L81: ```
L82: 
L83: The adapter installs Qwen command hooks in `.qwen/settings.json`. The stable Entire sidecar transcript lives in a repo-scoped OS temp directory, with a small `.entire/tmp/<session>.json` marker for Entire session discovery. Qwen Code must execute actual tools for checkpoints; local model backends that only print XML-style tool tags as text will not fire Qwen `PostToolUse` hooks.
L84: 
L85: ### Grok Build
L86: 
L87: Grok support targets the Grok Build CLI:
L88: 
L89: ```bash
L90: cd agents/entire-agent-grok
L91: mise run build
L92: cp entire-agent-grok ~/.local/bin/
L93: 
L94: cd /path/to/your/repo
L95: entire enable --agent grok --telemetry=false
L96: grok "Create hello.txt with hello world"
L97: ```
L98: 
L99: The adapter installs Grok command hooks in `.grok/hooks/entire.json` and reads native transcripts from `~/.grok/sessions/<encoded-cwd>/<session-id>/chat_history.jsonl`. Project hooks require folder trust (`/hooks-trust` or `--trust`) before they execute, and until the folder is trusted Grok skips them silently, so nothing is captured.
L100: 
L101: Restored sessions can be resumed with `grok --resume <session-id>`, but not at full fidelity: Grok's `encrypted_content` reasoning state is stripped before storage, so a resumed session replays the conversation without its prior reasoning context. Sessions captured before this behaviour shipped cannot be resumed at all. See the [agent README](agents/entire-agent-grok/README.md#session-restore-and-resume).
L102: 
L103: ### Hermes Agent
L104: 
L105: Hermes support uses an embedded standalone observer plugin and requires an explicit `HERMES_HOME`; it never falls back to the default profile. The observer stores a repository-scoped sanitized JSONL transcript and intentionally excludes system/developer prompts, memory, full history, platform identifiers, environment data, secrets, tool arguments, and raw tool results.
L106: 
L107: ```bash
L108: cd agents/entire-agent-hermes
L109: mise run build
L110: export PATH="$PWD:$PATH"
L111: export HERMES_HOME=/absolute/path/to/a/hermes/profile
L112: 
L113: cd /path/to/your/repo
L114: entire enable --agent hermes --telemetry=false
L115: hermes --yolo --ignore-rules -z "Create hello.txt with hello world"
L116: ```
L117: 
L118: One profile can register multiple repositories. Uninstalling the adapter from one repository leaves unrelated Hermes plugins and other repository registrations intact. See the [Hermes adapter README](agents/entire-agent-hermes/) for the disposable-profile verification flow.
L119: 
L120: ## Building a New External Agent
L121: 
L122: This repo includes a skill that guides you through building a new external agent with two test layers:
L123: 
L124: 1. **Protocol compliance** — generic subcommand coverage from [`entireio/external-agents-tests`](https://github.com/entireio/external-agents-tests)
L125: 2. **Lifecycle integration** — repo-local `e2e/` tests that exercise `entire enable`, prompt execution, checkpoints, and rewind
L126: 3. **Implementation** — build the binary until both layers pass, then add unit tests
L127: 
L128: ### Getting Started — Zero Setup
L129: 
L130: Clone the repo and open it in your AI coding tool. Each tool auto-discovers the skill with no additional configuration:
L131: 
L132: | Tool | How it discovers | What to say |
L133: |------|-----------------|-------------|
L134: | **Claude Code** | `.claude/skills/` directory | `/entire-external-agent` |
L135: | **Codex** | `AGENTS.md` at project root | "Build an external agent" |
L136: | **Cursor** | `.cursor/rules/` directory | "Build an external agent" |
L137: | **OpenCode** | `.opencode/plugins/` auto-loaded | "Build an external agent" |
L138: 
L139: The skill files live in `.claude/skills/entire-external-agent/` if you want to read the details.
L140: 
L141: ## Testing
L142: 
L143: Testing is intentionally split:
L144: 
L145: - **Generic protocol checks** run in GitHub Actions via [`entireio/external-agents-tests`](https://github.com/entireio/external-agents-tests). The workflow builds each `entire-agent-*` binary in this repo and runs the shared compliance suite against it.
L146: - **Agent unit/build checks** run in GitHub Actions for every `agents/entire-agent-*` directory discovered at runtime.
L147: - **Lifecycle tests** stay in this repo's [`e2e/`](e2e/) harness. These verify the parts that depend on Entire itself and on the real agent CLI: prompt execution, hook installation after `entire enable`, checkpoint creation, rewind behavior, and interactive sessions.
L148: - **Unit tests** live with each agent implementation under [`agents/`](agents/).
L149: 
L150: ### Running Tests
L151: 
L152: ```bash
L153: # Run default test suite for all agents
L154: mise run test
L155: 
L156: # Same as test, kept for explicit CI-style naming
L157: mise run test:ci
L158: 
L159: # Run lifecycle integration tests from this repo
L160: mise run test:e2e
L161: 
L162: # Same as test:e2e, kept as the explicit name
L163: mise run test:e2e:lifecycle
L164: ```
L165: 
L166: Protocol compliance runs in CI through [`.github/workflows/protocol-compliance.yml`](.github/workflows/protocol-compliance.yml).
L167: 
L168: For a newly added agent to be picked up automatically by local root tasks and CI, add `agents/entire-agent-<name>/mise.toml` with `build` and `test` tasks. The shared runner falls back to Go defaults when `go.mod` exists, but the `mise` tasks are the contract for non-standard setups.
L169: 
L170: ### Lifecycle Harness Architecture
L171: 
L172: The lifecycle harness auto-discovers and builds all agents in `agents/` via `TestMain`:
L173: 
L174: | File | Purpose |
L175: |------|---------|
L176: | `e2e/setup_test.go` | `TestMain` entry point — discovers agents, builds binaries, configures PATH |
L177: | `e2e/lifecycle_test.go` | Shared lifecycle scenarios run against every registered agent |
L178: | `e2e/agents/` | Agent adapters for the real CLIs used during lifecycle tests |
L179: | `e2e/entire/` | Entire CLI wrappers used by lifecycle assertions |
L180: | `e2e/testutil/` | Repo setup, artifact capture, git helpers, and checkpoint assertions |
L181: 
L182: ### Environment Variables
L183: 
L184: | Variable | Description |
L185: |----------|-------------|
L186: | `E2E_ENTIRE_BIN` | Path to the `entire` binary (defaults to `entire` from PATH) |
L187: | `E2E_AGENT` | Filter lifecycle runs to a single registered agent |
L188: | `E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR` | Override lifecycle artifact output directory |
L189: | `E2E_KEEP_REPOS` | Preserve temp repos for debugging |
L190: | `E2E_CONCURRENT_TEST_LIMIT` | Override the per-agent lifecycle concurrency limit |
L191: | `QWEN_E2E` | Set to `1` with `E2E_AGENT=qwen` to run live Qwen Code lifecycle tests |
L192: | `HERMES_E2E` | Set to `1` with `E2E_AGENT=hermes` and an explicit disposable `HERMES_HOME` to run live Hermes lifecycle tests |
L193: 
L194: ## Repository Layout
L195: 
L196: ```
L197: agents/                          # Standalone external agent projects
L198:   entire-agent-kiro/             # Kiro agent (Go binary)
L199:   entire-agent-amp/              # Amp agent (Go binary)
L200:   entire-agent-langgraph/        # LangGraph callback bridge (Python wrapper)
L201:   entire-agent-crewai/           # CrewAI listener bridge (Python wrapper)
L202:   entire-agent-qwen/             # Qwen Code agent (Go binary)
L203:   entire-agent-omp/              # Oh My Pi agent (Go binary)
L204:   entire-agent-kilo/             # Kilo agent (Go binary)
L205:   entire-agent-hermes/           # Hermes Agent (Go binary + embedded observer plugin)
L206:   entire-agent-sarvam/           # Sarvam Code agent (Go binary)
L207: e2e/                             # Lifecycle integration harness
L208: .github/workflows/               # CI, including protocol compliance via external-agents-tests
L209: .claude/skills/entire-external-agent/  # Skill files (research, test-writer, implementer)
L210: AGENTS.md                        # Codex auto-discovery
L211: .cursor/rules/                   # Cursor auto-discovery
L212: .opencode/plugins/               # OpenCode auto-discovery
L213: ```

(End of file - total 213 lines)
